title: English Practice Exam 2024
description: English Practice Exam 2024 - 100 multiple choice questions. Ethiopian national exam preparation material.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a present participle functioning as part of a verb phrase?
options: She is studying for the examination.
Having finished the work, he left.
questions.explanation: In "is studying," the present participle studying combines with is to form the present continuous tense.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses a past participle as an adjective rather than as part of a passive construction?
options: The window was broken by the boys.
The exhausted runner collapsed near the finish line.
questions.explanation: "Exhausted" describes the noun runner and functions adjectivally.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "By the time we arrived, she had ___ the report."
questions.explanation: Past perfect requires had + past participle. The V3 form of write is written.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a present participle in a continuous tense?
questions.explanation: A continuous tense requires a form of be followed by the present participle.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She has went to the library.
She has gone to the library.
She has going to the library.
She is gone to the library.
questions.explanation: After has, the past participle is required. The V3 form of go is gone.

questions.questionText: In the sentence "The frightened students left the room," what does "frightened" mainly express?
questions.explanation: The -ed participle adjective frightened describes those experiencing the feeling.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an -ing adjective describing something that causes a feeling?
questions.explanation: "Fascinating" describes the documentary as the thing causing interest.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The workers ___ the building when the alarm sounded."
questions.explanation: The past continuous uses were + present participle, showing an action in progress.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a past participle used in passive voice?
questions.explanation: "Were completed" is a passive construction using be + past participle.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "Having ___ the examination, the students left the hall."
questions.explanation: A perfect participle has the structure having + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a participial phrase with an active meaning?
options: Shocked by the news, he remained silent.
Built in the nineteenth century, the house is famous.
Walking through the market, she noticed a familiar face.
Surrounded by trees, the house looked peaceful.
questions.explanation: "Walking through the market" has an active meaning because the subject performs the action.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a participial phrase with a passive or resulting meaning?
options: Running toward the station, he dropped his bag.
Looking through the window, she saw the accident.
Exhausted after the journey, they went to bed.
Crossing the bridge, we heard a loud noise.
questions.explanation: "Exhausted" expresses a resulting condition of the subject.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct reduction of: "Because she was tired, she went home."
questions.explanation: The clause can be reduced to "Being tired," because the understood subject is the same.

questions.questionText: Choose the best reduced form of: "After he finished his work, he went home."
options: Having finished his work, he went home.
Finished his work, he went home.
Having finish his work, he went home.
Finishing had his work, he went home.
questions.explanation: "Having finished" shows that finishing occurred before going home.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a passive perfect participle?
options: Having completed the task, she rested.
Having been warned about the danger, they left.
Being warned about the danger, they left.
Warning about the danger, they left.
questions.explanation: Having been + V3 forms a passive perfect participle.

questions.questionText: Which structure correctly forms a perfect participle?
questions.explanation: The perfect participle is formed with having + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a dangling participle?
options: Walking to school, I saw the accident.
Walking to school, the rain suddenly started.
Shocked by the news, she left immediately.
Having finished the test, he submitted it.
questions.explanation: The phrase "Walking to school" incorrectly suggests that the rain was walking.

questions.questionText: Which revision correctly fixes the dangling participle? "Driving to work, the traffic suddenly became heavy."
options: Driving to work, the traffic became heavy.
Driving to work, I encountered heavy traffic.
Driving to work, heavy traffic was encountered.
Driving to work, there was heavy traffic.
questions.explanation: The subject of the participial phrase must logically be the subject of the main clause.

questions.questionText: Which form is the correct past participle of "write"?
questions.explanation: Write has the forms write, wrote, written.

questions.questionText: Which form is the correct past participle of "break"?
questions.explanation: The V3 form of break is broken.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the past participle of "see"?
questions.explanation: After has, the V3 form seen is required.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The students were boring by the lecture.
The students were bored by the lecture.
The students were bore by the lecture.
The students were boring with the lecture.
questions.explanation: The students experienced boredom, so the -ed adjective bored is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct adjective: "The professor gave a very ___ explanation."
questions.explanation: The explanation causes confusion, so confusing is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct adjective: "The students were completely ___ by the instructions."
questions.explanation: The students experienced confusion, so confused is correct.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an -ing adjective?
options: I was exciting by the result.
I was exciting about the result.
questions.explanation: The result causes excitement, so exciting describes it correctly.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an -ed adjective?
options: The travelers were frightening by the storm.
The travelers were frightened by the storm.
The travelers were frighten by the storm.
The travelers were frightening the storm.
questions.explanation: The travelers experienced fear, so frightened is correct.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a present participle as an adjective?
questions.explanation: "Sleeping" modifies child and functions as an adjective.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a past participle functioning adjectivally?
options: The car was damaging the wall.
The car has damage the wall.
questions.explanation: "Damaged" describes the condition of the car.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The letter ___ yesterday has already been sent."
questions.explanation: "Written yesterday" is a past participle phrase modifying letter.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The man ___ near the entrance is our teacher."
questions.explanation: "Standing near the entrance" is a present participial phrase modifying man.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the future continuous tense?
options: She will be studying at midnight.
She will have studying at midnight.
She will be studied at midnight.
questions.explanation: Future continuous uses will be + present participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect tense?
options: They will have completed the project.
They will have completing the project.
They will be completed the project.
They will have complete the project.
questions.explanation: Future perfect uses will have + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses perfect passive voice?
questions.explanation: Perfect passive requires have + been + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses passive voice in the present tense?
options: The reports are written every Friday.
The reports are writing every Friday.
The reports have write every Friday.
questions.explanation: Present passive uses am/is/are + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses passive voice in the past tense?
options: The bridge was built last year.
The bridge was building last year.
The bridge had build last year.
The bridge was build last year.
questions.explanation: Past passive uses was/were + V3.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a participle but not a participial phrase?
options: Walking along the road, he saw a bird.
Having finished the work, she left.
Shocked by the news, he remained silent.
questions.explanation: "Broken" is a single participle functioning as an adjective, not a participial phrase.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a present participle phrase?
options: Written in English, the notice was easy to understand.
Having completed the work, she rested.
Looking out of the window, he noticed the storm.
Shocked by the result, they remained silent.
questions.explanation: "Looking out of the window" begins with a present participle and functions as a phrase.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a past participle phrase?
options: Running toward the station, she dropped her bag.
Surrounded by mountains, the village is beautiful.
Studying all night, she became tired.
questions.explanation: "Surrounded by mountains" begins with the past participle surrounded.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct reduction: "Because he was shocked by the news, he left immediately."
options: Shocking by the news, he left immediately.
Shocked by the news, he left immediately.
Being shock by the news, he left immediately.
Having shock by the news, he left immediately.
questions.explanation: The passive condition can be reduced to the past participle phrase "Shocked by the news."

questions.questionText: Choose the best reduction: "After she had completed the assignment, she submitted it."
options: Completing had the assignment, she submitted it.
Having completed the assignment, she submitted it.
Completed the assignment, she submitted it.
Having complete the assignment, she submitted it.
questions.explanation: Having + V3 clearly shows that completion occurred before submission.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best expresses two sequential actions using a perfect participle?
options: Having eaten dinner, we watched a movie.
Eating dinner, we had watched a movie.
Having eat dinner, we watched a movie.
Eaten dinner, we watching a movie.
questions.explanation: "Having eaten" shows that dinner occurred before watching the movie.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly expresses a prior passive action?
options: Having warned about the danger, they left.
Having been warned about the danger, they left.
Having been warning about the danger, they left.
Having warned by the danger, they left.
questions.explanation: The subject received the warning, so the passive form having been warned is required.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an incorrect participle?
questions.explanation: The V3 form of go is gone, not went.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an incorrect use of an -ing/-ed adjective?
options: The students were interested in science.
I was bored during the speech.
I was boring during the speech.
questions.explanation: The speaker experiences boredom, so bored is needed.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The movie causes fear, so frightening is the appropriate adjective.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The children were frightening by the story.
The children were frightened by the story.
The children were frighten by the story.
The children were frightening the story.
questions.explanation: The children experience fear, so frightened is correct.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the past participle of "take" correctly?
questions.explanation: The V3 form of take is taken.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the past participle of "eat" correctly?
questions.explanation: The past participle of eat is eaten.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the past participle of "speak" correctly?
options: He has spoke to the manager.
He has spoken to the manager.
He is spoke to the manager.
He had speaking to the manager.
questions.explanation: The V3 form of speak is spoken.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses a regular past participle correctly?
questions.explanation: The regular past participle of clean is cleaned.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a participle after "have"?
questions.explanation: Have is followed by the past participle in perfect constructions.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a participle after "be" in a continuous tense?
questions.explanation: Continuous constructions use be + present participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a participle after "be" in passive voice?
questions.explanation: Passive voice uses be + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains both a perfect auxiliary and a past participle?
questions.explanation: "Has written" is a present perfect construction.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains both a form of be and a present participle?
questions.explanation: "Are completing" uses be + present participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains both a form of be and a past participle?
questions.explanation: "Was closed" is a passive construction using be + past participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly distinguishes "interesting" from "interested"?
options: The students were interesting in biology.
Biology was interested to the students.
The biology lecture was interesting, and the students were interested.
The students were interesting because they felt interest.
questions.explanation: The lecture causes interest, while the students experience interest.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly distinguishes "boring" from "bored"?
options: The audience was boring by the speech.
The long speech was boring, and the audience was bored.
The audience was boring because the speech caused boredom.
questions.explanation: The speech causes boredom, while the audience experiences it.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The ___ students listened carefully to the professor."
questions.explanation: The students experience interest, so interested is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The professor gave an ___ lecture."
questions.explanation: The lecture causes interest, so interesting is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The ___ instructions confused everyone."
questions.explanation: The instructions cause confusion, so confusing is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: "The students looked ___ after reading the instructions."
questions.explanation: The students experienced confusion, so confused describes them.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct subject for the participial phrase?
options: Running down the street, the accident was seen by John.
Running down the street, John saw the accident.
Running down the street, there was an accident.
Running down the street, the accident happened.
questions.explanation: John is the person running, so he must be the logical subject.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a dangling participle?
options: After finishing the exam, I left the room.
Having studied carefully, she passed the test.
While walking home, the rain began suddenly.
Shocked by the result, he said nothing.
questions.explanation: The rain cannot logically be walking home, so the participial phrase dangles.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly fixes the dangling participle: "After studying all night, the examination seemed easy."?
options: After studying all night, the examination seemed easy to me.
After studying all night, I found the examination easy.
After studying all night, the examination was easy.
After studying all night, there was an easy examination.
questions.explanation: I am the one who studied, so I should be the subject of the main clause.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Having finished the work, the computer was turned off.
Having finished the work, Maria turned off the computer.
Having finish the work, Maria turned off the computer.
Having finishing the work, Maria turned off the computer.
questions.explanation: Maria performed the action of finishing, and having + V3 is correctly formed.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a past participle phrase to express a resulting condition?
options: Exhausted after the journey, they went straight to bed.
Exhausting after the journey, they went straight to bed.
Exhausted after the journey, the bed went straight to them.
Having exhaust after the journey, they went to bed.
questions.explanation: Exhausted describes the resulting condition of the travelers.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an active present participle phrase?
options: Surrounded by trees, the house looked peaceful.
Built in 1900, the house is historic.
Looking through the window, she noticed the storm.
Shocked by the news, she left.
questions.explanation: She performs the action of looking, so the active -ing participle is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a passive past participle phrase?
options: Walking through the forest, he heard birds.
Surrounded by mountains, the village looked beautiful.
Having walked through the forest, he rested.
Running through the forest, he became tired.
questions.explanation: The village is surrounded by mountains, giving the phrase a passive meaning.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct completion: "___ by the sudden noise, the baby began to cry."
questions.explanation: The baby experiences fear, so the past participle frightened is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct completion: "___ everyone in the room, the announcement caused immediate concern."
questions.explanation: The announcement causes fear, so frightening is appropriate.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses "having been"?
options: Having been warned, the hikers changed their route.
Having been warning, the hikers changed their route.
Having been warn, the hikers changed their route.
Having been warned, the route changed the hikers.
questions.explanation: Having been + V3 expresses a prior passive action received by the subject.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct participle form after "having"?
options: Having wrote the letter, she left.
Having written the letter, she left.
Having writing the letter, she left.
Having write the letter, she left.
questions.explanation: Having must be followed by the past participle written.

questions.questionText: Which sentence has the correct participle form after "has"?
questions.explanation: Has is followed by the past participle written.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "gone"?
options: He has gone to Addis Ababa.
He has went to Addis Ababa.
He is gone to Addis Ababa.
He had going to Addis Ababa.
questions.explanation: Gone is the past participle of go and follows has in the present perfect.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "seen"?
questions.explanation: Seen is the V3 form of see.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "broken"?
options: The glass is breaking by him.
questions.explanation: Broken is the past participle of break.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "spoken"?
questions.explanation: Spoken is the V3 form of speak.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "taken"?
questions.explanation: Taken is the past participle of take.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "eaten"?
questions.explanation: Eaten is the past participle of eat.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "written" in passive voice?
questions.explanation: Passive voice requires was + V3, and written is the V3 form.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the participle "completed" in passive voice?
options: The assignment was completed on time.
The assignment was completing on time.
The assignment was complete on time.
The assignment has completing on time.
questions.explanation: Was + completed forms the past passive.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an error involving the continuous tense?
options: They were studying for the examination.
questions.explanation: The continuous tense requires a form of be before the -ing participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an error involving the perfect tense?
options: He will have finished by noon.
questions.explanation: Has must be followed by the past participle written, not V2 wrote.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains an error involving passive voice?
options: The letters are written every day.
questions.explanation: The passive requires the V3 form written, not the V2 form wrote.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best demonstrates that an -ing adjective describes a cause?
options: The students felt excited because they were exciting.
questions.explanation: The competition causes excitement, so exciting describes it.

questions.questionText: Which sentence best demonstrates that an -ed adjective describes an experiencer?
options: The students were surprised by the result.
The students were surprising by the result.
questions.explanation: The students experience surprise, so surprised is correct.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The frightened noise made the child cry.
The frightening noise made the child cry.
The frighten noise made the child cry.
questions.explanation: The noise causes fear, so frightening correctly modifies noise.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The frightened child ran away from the frightening dog.
The frightening child ran away from the frightened dog.
The frightened child ran away from the frightened dog.
The frightening child ran away from the frightening dog.
questions.explanation: The child experiences fear, while the dog causes fear.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reduces the clause "Because they were exhausted after the journey, they went to bed early"?
options: Exhausting after the journey, they went to bed early.
Exhausted after the journey, they went to bed early.
Having exhaust after the journey, they went to bed early.
Being exhaust after the journey, they went to bed early.
questions.explanation: Exhausted expresses the resulting condition of the same subject.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reduces "Because the village is surrounded by mountains, it is difficult to reach"?
options: Surrounding by mountains, the village is difficult to reach.
Surrounded by mountains, the village is difficult to reach.
Having surround by mountains, the village is difficult to reach.
Surrounding mountains, the village is difficult to reach.
questions.explanation: The village receives the action, so the passive participle surrounded is needed.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly reduces "After they had been warned about the danger, they left immediately"?
options: Having warned about the danger, they left immediately.
Having been warned about the danger, they left immediately.
Having been warning about the danger, they left immediately.
Warned having been about the danger, they left immediately.
questions.explanation: The subjects received the warning before leaving, requiring the passive perfect participle.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a present participle to shorten a relative clause?
options: The man who is standing outside is my uncle.
The man standing outside is my uncle.
The man stood outside is my uncle.
The man is standing outside is my uncle.
questions.explanation: "Standing outside" reduces the active relative clause "who is standing outside."

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a past participle to shorten a passive relative clause?
options: The books which were written by the professor are valuable.
The books writing by the professor are valuable.
The books written by the professor are valuable.
The books were written by the professor are valuable.
questions.explanation: "Written by the professor" reduces the passive relative clause.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a participle functioning as an adjective?
questions.explanation: "Running" modifies water and functions adjectivally.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a participle functioning as part of a verb phrase?
options: The exciting game attracted many people.
questions.explanation: "Were playing" is a verb phrase containing the present participle playing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a past participle functioning as part of a verb phrase rather than simply as an adjective?
options: The documents were signed by the director.
questions.explanation: "Were signed" forms a passive verb phrase.

questions.questionText: Which sentence contains a perfect participle showing that the first action happened before the second?
options: Studying hard, she passed the examination.
Having studied hard, she passed the examination.
She was studying hard when she passed.
questions.explanation: "Having studied" explicitly presents studying as preceding passing.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a participial phrase without changing the logical subject?
options: Looking at the map, the road seemed confusing.
Looking at the map, I found the road confusing.
Looking at the map, there was a road.
Looking at the map, the directions were difficult.
questions.explanation: I am the one looking at the map, so I must be the logical subject.

questions.questionText: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Having finished the examination, the students left quietly.
Having finish the examination, the students left quietly.
Having finishing the examination, the students left quietly.
Having finished the examination, the examination left quietly.
questions.explanation: Having + V3 is correctly formed, and the students logically performed the action.
